Slipstream / live execution costs
Live History Methodology Data (CSV) API & MCP GitHub

Buying or selling crypto in one big order pushes the price against you, and every exchange also takes a fee.

Every hour, Slipstream paper-trades a small order on the live Kraken and Coinbase order books, with four splitting strategies, and records what each one really cost, fees included.

No real money moves; the prices are real, only the fills are simulated.

Code, tests and methodology: github.com/yandouziyassine/slipstream

Use it yourself

The same engine that runs these hourly tests will be open to use directly. Paper trading only; nothing can place a real order.

Public API coming soon

Ask for the cheapest way to buy or sell right now and get the route, the all-in cost and the estimated saving back in milliseconds.

MCP server for AI assistants coming soon

Add one URL to Claude or another MCP-capable assistant, and it can answer "what's the cheapest way to buy 0.5 BTC right now?" with live, measured numbers instead of a guess.

Want early access or to follow progress? Watch the GitHub repository.

How to read this. "All-in" is what a trade paid above the market price at the moment the order started, in basis points, fees included. A routing gain of 0.00 is an honest result: one exchange was simply cheaper for the whole order.
Not financial advice. Research and education only. These are paper trades on real public prices; the simulated fills do not consume order-book liquidity, so results can look slightly better than a real fill would. See the methodology page for the full list of limits.
